'''Kirill Yuryevich Yeskov''' ({{langx|ru|Кирилл Юрьевич Еськов}}; born 16 September 1956, Moscow), also transliterated '''Kiril Eskov''', is a Russian writer, [[biologist]] and [[paleontologist]]. As an author he is known for ''[[The Gospel of Afranius]]'' in which he presents an atheistic interpretation of the events of the Gospel, and ''[[The Last Ringbearer]]'' in which he retells [[J. R. R. Tolkien]]'s ''[[The Lord of the Rings]]'' from a [[Mordor]]ian point of view.

==Career==

=== In biology ===

Yeskov graduated from the Department of Biology of [[Moscow State University]] in 1979. In 1986 he defended a dissertation for the [[Kandidat|Candidate of Biological Sciences]] at the A.N. Severtsov Institute of Animal Evolutionary Morphology and Ecology of the [[USSR Academy of Sciences]], the theme being "[[Spider]]s of Northern [[Siberia]] ([[horology]] analysis)".<ref>{{Cite web |url= http://artedi.fish.washington.edu/okhotskia/ikip/results/Bios/eskov.html |title=Kirill Y. Eskov |publisher=[[International Kuril Island Project|IKIP]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070426231922/http://artedi.fish.washington.edu/okhotskia/ikip/Results/Bios/eskov.html |archive-date= 26 April 2007 |department=Biographies}}</ref> His main scientific interests as a biologist focus on the [[spider]]s of Siberia and the [[Russian Far East]] and, as a paleontologist, on the [[Paleozoic]] and [[Cenozoic]] [[Era (geology)|eras]]. {{As of| 2008}} he is the Senior Researcher at the Laboratory of [[Arthropods]] of the [[Paleontological Institute of Russian Academy of Sciences]] and vice-president of the Eurasian Arachnological Society. He has worked at the institute since 1988. {{As of|2002}} he had 86 scientific publications.

Yeskov has discovered several new genera of spiders. Among seven that he discovered in 1988 is ''[[Kikimora palustris]]'' <small>Eskov, 1988</small><ref>[http://research.amnh.org/entomology/spiders/catalog/LINYPHIIDAE.html World Spider Catalog - Linyphiidae]</ref> It belongs to the family [[Linyphiidae]], and is found in [[Russia]] and [[Finland]]. The name translates from [[Latin language|Latin]] as "marsh Kikimora". ([[Kikimora]] is a female spirit in [[Slavic mythology]] and the Russian phrase ''кикимора болотная'' (''kikimora bolotnaya'', "marsh kikimora") is well known in the [[Russian language|Russian]] language.) 
He has named a [[genus]] of linyphiid spiders  ''[[Sauron (spider)|Sauron]]'' after the Tolkien character<!--and see his book below...-->.<ref name=Esko1995>{{cite journal |last1=Eskov |first1=Kirill Y. |author1-link=Kirill Eskov |last2=Marusik |first2=Y. M. |year=1995 |title=On the spiders from Saur Mt. range, eastern Kazakhstan (Arachnida: Araneae) |journal=Beiträge zur Araneologie |pages=55–94 |volume=4 |issue=1994}}</ref>

He is the author of the book ''History of the Earth and its lifeforms'' ({{langx |ru| Удивительная палеонтология: История Земли и жизни на ней}}, Moscow, 2008), intended as a biology textbook for high schools.

In recent years, Yeskov has been working on [[phylogeny]] of [[trapdoor spider]]s and evolution of [[trichobothria]] in [[spider]]s in general.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Eskov |first1=K.Y. |last2=Zonstein |first2=S.L. |last3=Marusik |first3=Y.M. |date=2024 |title=On the liphistiomorph trichobothria and the significance of their structure for tracking the bothria evolution in the order Araneae |journal=[[Israel Journal of Entomology]] |volume=53 |pages=93–112 |issn=2224-6304 |language=en |url=https://ij-entomology.online/ojs/index.php/ije/article/view/224}}{{open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Eskov |first1=K.Y. |last2=Guadanucci |first2=J.P.L. |last3=Indicatti |first3=R.P.|last4=Marusik |first4=Y.M. |last5=Zonstein |first5=S.L. |date=2026 |title=A comparative morphology of trichobothrial bases in mygalomorph spiders and its significance for the phylogeny and system of the infraorder (Arachnida: Araneae: Mygalomorphae) |journal=[[Israel Journal of Entomology]] |volume=55 |pages=73–146 |issn=2224-6304 |language=en |url=https://ij-entomology.online/ojs/index.php/ije/article/view/377}}{{open access}}</ref>

=== As an author ===

As a fiction writer, Yeskov has published several books, one of the best-known being ''[[The Last Ringbearer]]'' ({{langx|ru| Последний кольценосец}}), an alternative retelling of (or sequel to) [[J. R. R. Tolkien]]'s ''[[The Lord of the Rings]]'', as told from the point of view of [[Sauron]]'s forces in light of the [[proverb]] "[[History is written by the victors]]."<ref name="Salon">{{Cite web |url=https://www.salon.com/2011/02/15/last_ringbearer/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111103091522/http://www.salon.com/2011/02/15/last_ringbearer/ |url-status=live |archive-date=3 November 2011 |title=Middle-earth according to Mordor |last=Miller |first=Laura |author-link=Laura Miller (writer) |date=15 February 2011 |website=[[Salon.com]] |language=en |access-date=23 April 2019}}</ref> The book was "published to acclaim" in his homeland in 1999. Translations of the book have also appeared in other European nations, but fear of the vigilant and litigious [[Tolkien Estate|Tolkien estate]] has heretofore prevented its publication in English."<ref name="Salon" /> In late 2010, however, an English translation approved by Yeskov was posted on [[LiveJournal]].<ref name="Salon" /> The American journalist [[Laura Miller (writer)|Laura Miller]] characterised ''The Last Ringbearer'' as "a well-written, energetic adventure yarn that offers an intriguing gloss on what some critics have described as the overly simplistic morality of Tolkien's masterpiece."<ref name="Salon" />

Other books by Yeskov include ''[[The Gospel of Afranius]]'' ({{langx|ru| Евангелие от Афрания}}), a [[dramatic portrayal of Jesus]]. In this work he presents a demythologised account of the events of the [[Synoptic Gospels|Gospels]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mina |first=Mikhail |date=30 April 1998 |title=In retrospect by Mikhail Mina |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/31855 |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |language=en |volume=392 |issue=6679 |pages=884 |doi=10.1038/31855 |bibcode=1998Natur.392..884M |s2cid=35300944 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
